title: Isolation, Culture, and Functional Analysis of Murine Thermogenic Adipocytes
protocol: Isolate stromal vascular fraction from murine adipose tissue.
Seed pre-adipocytes into Seahorse XF96 cell culture microplates.
Differentiate seeded cells into mature adipocytes.
Perform oxygen consumption assay according to instructions for respirometry part.
Euthanize mice by CO2 asphyxiation.
Dissect interscapular brown adipose tissue and/or inguinal white adipose tissue carefully.
Rinse adipose tissue with PBS-A.
Remove remaining connective tissue and muscle tissue from the dissected tissue.
Cover the tissue with PBS-A to prevent drying out; process quickly in a sterile manner.
Mince adipose tissue into small pieces (<1–2 mm3) using scissors.
Transfer minced tissue into a 15 mL tube.
Add 7 mL of collagenase solution for digestion.
Place the digestion reaction tube horizontally into an orbital shaker.
Incubate the tube at 37°C (120–180 rpm) for 45 min to 1 h 15 min.
Vigorously shake the tube by hand for 10 s every 15 min during incubation.
Filter the mixture through a 250 μm nylon mesh and capture the flow-through in a new 15 ml tube.
Rinse the digestion reaction tube with 7 ml of wash buffer, then filter through the same nylon mesh.
Combine the filtered flow-through from previous steps.
Centrifuge the combined solution at 250 × g for 5 min at 18°C–26°C (room temperature).
Invert the tube several times to break up the fat layer floating on top before centrifuging again.
Completely remove the fat layer and supernatant, without disturbing the cell pellet.
Add 1 mL of wash medium and break up the cell pellet by carefully pipetting up and down.
Incubate for 3–5 min at room temperature (optional: use red blood cell lysis buffer instead of wash medium).
Add 13 mL of wash buffer and centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Completely remove the supernatant, without disturbing the cell pellet.
Add 1 mL of growth medium and resuspend cells by carefully pipetting up and down.
Mix cells in the reservoir by gently pipetting up and down or shaking the reservoir to ensure thorough resuspension.
Seed 80 μL of cell suspension per well into a Seahorse XF96 cell culture microplate using a multichannel pipette.
Do not seed cells in the four background correction wells (A1, A12, H1, H12).
Add growth medium without cells in these four background correction wells.
If the experimental design does not require a whole 96-well plate, add PBS or growth medium in the empty wells.
Let the plate rest at 18°C–26°C (room temperature) in the cell culture hood for 1 h after seeding.
Seed SVF cells into a defined number of fat depots or wells of a cell culture plate.
Ensure that SVF cells reach 30%–40% confluence within 72 hours after seeding.
For established brown or brite adipocyte cell lines, seed 10,000 cells per well into a Seahorse XF96 cell culture microplate.
Remove growth medium using a vacuum manifold adapter at least 6 hours post-seeding.
Add 150 μL of fresh growth medium with a multichannel pipette.
Process one half or even one third of the microplate at a time.
Remove most but not all of the medium from each well, leaving around 20 μL behind.
Change the growth medium every other day until cells reach 80%–100% confluency (termed “day 0”).
On day 0, remove the growth medium and add 150 μL of induction medium per well.
Prepare induction medium freshly prior to usage.
On day 2, remove the induction medium and add 150 μL of differentiation medium per well.
Change differentiation medium every other day until the cells are fully differentiated on day 8.
Add 8 mL of growth medium (iBAT) or 6 mL of growth medium (iWAT).
Filter the cell suspension through a 40 μm cell strainer into a 15 mL tube.
Repetitively mix the cells in the reservoir by gently pipetting up and down to ensure thorough resuspension.
Seed 2 mL of cell suspension per well into a 6-well cell culture plate (4 wells for iBAT and 3 wells for iWAT).
Carefully shake the plate backward and forward, then left and right.
Let the plate rest at 18°C–26°C in the cell culture hood for 10 min after seeding to allow equal distribution of cells.
On the next day or at least 6 hours after seeding, carefully remove the growth medium from wells.
Wash the cells twice with prewarmed PBS.
Completely remove PBS and add 2 mL of fresh growth medium.
Change growth medium every other day until the cells reach 80%-100% confluency (termed “day 0”).
On day 0, remove growth medium and add 2 mL of induction medium per well.
On day 2, remove induction medium and add 2 mL of differentiation medium per well.
Change differentiation medium every other day until cells are considered as differentiated on day 7.
Mix gently.
Add 25 μL of transfection mix per well into a Seahorse XF96 cell culture plate.
Incubate the plate for 20 min at 18°C–26°C in the cell culture hood.
Retrieve the 6-well cell culture plate from the cell culture incubator.
Wash cells twice with prewarmed PBS.
Remove PBS and add Trypsin-EDTA solution (for cells processed at day 0 and day 2), or Trypsin-EDTA-Collagenase solution (for cells processed at day 5).
Return the 6-well cell culture plate to the cell culture incubator for 2–10 min.
View cells under the microscope to ensure all cells are detached and floating.
Add growth medium (for cells processed at day 0) or differentiation medium (for cells processed at day 2 and day 5) without antibiotics to inactivate trypsin.
Centrifuge at 250 × g for 5 min at 18°C–26°C.
Completely remove the medium.
Plate at least 8 - 16 wells per negative control siRNA/siRNA treatment group.
Resuspend cells in an appropriate volume (125 μl per well) of growth medium without antibiotics and antifungal agents for day 0 processing.
Incubate the transfection mix at 18°C–26°C for at least 20 min.
Add 125 μl of cell suspension per well into a Seahorse XF96 cell culture plate.
Gently mix cells in the reservoir by pipetting up and down.
Place the cell culture plate toward the back of the incubator.
Carefully remove the medium 24 hours after seeding.
Add 150 μL of fresh induction or differentiation medium as appropriate.
Subject the cells to oxygen consumption analysis after another 48 hours.
Harvest cells for assessing knockdown efficiency if needed.
Hydrate the sensor cartridge for the Seahorse XF technology.
Create a Seahorse assay template.
Hydrate the Seahorse XFe96 sensor cartridge according to the manufacturer’s recommendations.
Aliquot 22 mL of Seahorse XF Calibrant into a 50 mL tube.
Incubate the 50 mL tube at 37°C in a laboratory non-CO2 incubator overnight.
Remove the sensor cartridge from the utility plate.
Add 200 μL of sterile water per well into the utility plate.
Lower the sensor cartridge onto the utility plate without applying force.
Incubate the sensor cartridge and utility plate at 37°C in a laboratory non-CO2 incubator overnight.
Complete the Agilent SeahorseXFe96 sensor cartridge hydration procedure.
Separate sensor cartridge from the utility plate.
Remove water from utility plate.
Add 200 μL of warm XF Calibrant per well into the utility plate.
Lower the sensor cartridge onto utility plate (do not apply force).
Incubate at 37°C in a laboratory incubator for around 1 h prior to loading the injection ports.
Aliquot 45 mL of respiration base medium into a 50 mL tube (used for wash steps later on).
Aliquot 22 mL of respiration base medium into a 50 mL tube (used for preparation of respiration assay medium later on).
Aliquot 13 mL of respiration base medium into a 15 mL tube (used for injections later on).
Incubate respiration base medium at 37°C until ready for use.
Prepare respiration assay medium by supplementing respiration base medium with essentially fatty acid free BSA.
Adjust pH of the respiration assay medium to 7.4 after bringing it to a final concentration of 2% (w/v) BSA and 37°C.
Incubate the final respiration assay medium at 37°C until ready for use.
Replace cell culture medium with weakly HEPES-buffered medium containing defined amount of BSA.
Remove all but 20 μL of differentiation medium using vacuum manifold adapter or multichannel pipette.
Add 200 μL of fresh respiration base medium with multichannel pipette.
Repeat removal and addition steps once more, leaving 20 μL behind after each wash.
Process one half or even one third of the microplate at a time.
Wash adherent cells in Seahorse XF96 cell culture microplates.
Add 160 μL of respiration assay medium to each well after the second wash.
Incubate the Seahorse XF96 cell culture microplate at 37°C for 60 minutes prior to the assay.
Mix Oligomycin with solvent to prepare a working solution.
Mix Isoproterenol with solvent to prepare a working solution.
Load prepared Oligomycin solution into the sensor cartridge’s injection port.
Load prepared Isoproterenol solution into the sensor cartridge’s injection port.
Prepare injection working solutions at a 10× concentration.
Increase the volume of injection working solution from port "A" to port "D" to ensure each compound reaches a 1× concentration in the microplate well.
Thaw appropriate volume of Oligomycin.
Thaw appropriate volume of FCCP.
Thaw appropriate volume of Antimycin A.
Protect Isoproterenol from light.
Prepare working solutions for each compound in respiration base medium.
Load sensor cartridge ports using a multichannel pipette and reagent reservoir.
Place the utility plate with the loaded sensor cartridge onto the instrument tray.
Start the assay around 40 minutes after placing the Seahorse XF96 cell culture microplate in an incubator.
Remove all loading guides and plastic lids before placing the sensor cartridge including the utility plate, and later the cell culture plate, onto the instrument tray.
Ensure that the utility plate fits properly on the instrument tray.
Check if everything is oriented correctly.
Replace the utility plate with the cell culture microplate when prompted.
Click Start to begin the assay.
The assay duration is approximately 2 hours.
Once the final measurement is completed, an “Unload Sensor Cartridge dialog” will be displayed.
Click Eject to remove the sensor cartridge and cell culture microplate.
Separate the sensor cartridge from the cell culture microplate.
Check the injection ports of the sensor cartridge for failed injections.
Note down any ports that were not completely emptied for subsequent data analysis.
